assessments.reasoning: The Default Value section defines default-value as an accessor for a symbol's default binding. Its setq-default rule evaluates each value form and assigns the result as the corresponding default, including when the current buffer has its own binding.

challenge.method: Compare the symbol argument with a setq-default value form, ordinary assignment in a buffer with a local value, the void-default note and buffers or frames with their own values.
challenge.results: The value-form evaluation is explicit. Updating a default can change what other buffers see while the current buffer keeps its local value. A void default can signal an error, and an existing default is required for a successful read.

limitations: This describes the normal read and assignment functions and leaves void-value errors, binding creation and frame-specific choices to their documented rules.
